2. Krauñca, as the name of a mountain, occurs only in the latest Vedic literature.
Foot notes taittirīya Āraṇyaka, i. 31, 2. See Weber, Indian Literature, 93; Indische Studien, 1, 78.

Krauñcikī-putra, ‘son of a female descendant of krauñca,’ is mentioned as a pupil of Vaiṭṭabhatīputra in the last vaṃśa (list of teachers) in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad.
Foot notes vaidabhṛtī-putra in the Mādhyaṃdina recension, vi. 4, 32.
vi. 5, 2 (kāṇva).

Krauṣṭuki, ‘descendant of Kroṣṭuka,’ is mentioned as a grammarian in the nirukta, the Bṛhaddevatā, and the chandas, but as an astrologer in a Pariśiṣṭa of the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes viii. 2.
iv. 137. Cf. Indische Studien, 1, 105.

Weber, Berlin Catalogue of Sanskrit MSS., 1, 94. See Bolling and von Negelein. The Pariśiṣṭas of the Atharvaveda, 2, 438 et seq., where in Pariśiṣṭa lxviii (Svapnādhyāyaḥ), i. 2; ii. 8, the name appears as Kroṣṭuki.
Cf. Weber, jyotiṣa, 12; Indian Literature, 61.
